ai.literal: Duty, they say, good things all, duty having known, perfection to those who undertake.
ai.translation: The wise say that all good deeds are a natural duty for those who know their obligations and commit themselves to noble excellence.
ai.modern: தம் கடமையை அறிந்து சான்றாண்மையை மேற்கொண்டு வாழ்பவர்களுக்கு, நல்ல செயல்கள் அனைத்தும் தாமே செய்ய வேண்டிய கடமை என்று அறிஞர்கள் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the mindset of those who strive for noble excellence. When a person understands their true responsibilities and commits to a noble life, they do not see good deeds as optional or extraordinary. Instead, they consider every good action as their basic, natural duty. The repetition of the word 'duty' emphasizes that excellence is a constant obligation to do what is right.

ai.literal: Goodness of character of the noble is goodness indeed; other goodness in any goodness included is not.
ai.translation: The true goodness of the noble is the goodness of their character. Any other kind of goodness is not counted as goodness at all.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்களின் உண்மையான நலம் என்பது அவர்களின் நற்குணங்களே ஆகும். மற்ற நலன்கள் எந்த வகையான நலத்திலும் சேராதவை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true wealth or goodness of noble people. It states that the excellence of their character is their only real goodness. Any other kind of advantage, such as physical beauty or material wealth, is not considered true goodness and does not belong in the category of real virtues. The word 'உள்ளதூஉம்' uses poetic lengthening to emphasize that other traits are absolutely not included in true goodness.

ai.literal: Love, shame, benevolence, compassion, with truthfulness, [these] five [are] perfection's planted pillars.
ai.translation: Love, a sense of shame, benevolence, compassion, and truthfulness are the five planted pillars that support perfection.
ai.modern: அன்பு, பழிக்கு நாணுதல், உலகத்தோடு ஒழுகும் ஒப்புரவு, இரக்கம், வாய்மை ஆகிய இந்த ஐந்தும் சான்றாண்மையைத் தாங்கி நிற்கும் தூண்களாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core components of noble perfection. It lists five essential virtues: 'அன்பு' (love), 'நாண்' (a sense of shame that shrinks from wrongdoing), 'ஒப்புரவு' (benevolence or social duty), 'கண்ணோட்டம்' (compassion or graciousness), and 'வாய்மை' (truthfulness). The word 'சால்' refers to perfection or nobility, which is described metaphorically as a structure supported by these five planted pillars ('ஊன்றிய தூண்'). By visualizing perfection as a building, the poet emphasizes that all five virtues are structurally necessary to uphold a noble character.

ai.literal: not killing, it has the goodness, penance; others' fault, not saying, it has the goodness, perfection.
ai.translation: Penance has the goodness of not killing. Perfection has the goodness of not speaking of others' faults.
ai.modern: உயிர்களைக் கொல்லாத நற்பண்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது தவம். அதுபோல, மற்றவர்களின் குற்றங்களைச் சொல்லாத நற்பண்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது சான்றாண்மை.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core virtues of two great ideals: penance and perfection. True penance (நோன்மை) is rooted in the goodness of not harming or killing any living being. Similarly, true perfection or nobility (சால்பு) is rooted in the goodness of not speaking about the faults of others. By placing these two side by side, the poet elevates the social virtue of refraining from gossip to the same level as the ascetic virtue of non-violence.

ai.literal: Of those who accomplish, the strength is being humble; that, for the noble ones, is the weapon that changes foes.
ai.translation: The true strength of capable people is their humility. For the noble, that same humility is the weapon that transforms their enemies.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்து முடிப்பவர்களின் உண்மையான வலிமை பணிவுடன் இருப்பதே ஆகும். சான்றோர்களுக்குப் பகைவர்களையும் நண்பர்களாக மாற்றும் ஆயுதம் அந்தப் பணிவே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines humility not as a weakness, but as the ultimate strength of capable individuals. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to those who can successfully accomplish tasks, and their true power ('ஆற்றல்') lies in being humble ('பணிதல்'). Furthermore, for the noble ('சான்றோர்'), this very humility acts as a powerful weapon ('படை') that disarms and transforms their enemies ('மாற்றாரை மாற்றும்').

ai.literal: For nobility, touchstone what, if asked: defeat, equal those-who-are-not from-even, accepting.
ai.translation: If asked what the touchstone of true nobility is, it is the willingness to accept defeat even from one's inferiors.
ai.modern: சான்றாண்மைக்கு உரைகல் எது என்றால், தமக்குச் சமம் இல்லாதவர்களிடமும் தோல்வியை ஏற்றுக்கொள்வதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate test of a noble character. The word 'கட்டளை' refers to a touchstone used to test the purity of gold, here representing the standard for testing nobility ('சால்பு'). The true measure of such greatness is the humility to accept defeat ('தோல்வி கொளல்'). Crucially, this defeat is accepted not just from equals or superiors, but even from those who are not one's equal ('துலை அல்லார்'), demonstrating profound modesty and the absence of ego.

ai.literal: Harm - even to those who did - sweet things indeed - if not done - what - use is it - nobility?
ai.translation: If one does not do good even to those who have done them harm, what is the use of nobility?
ai.modern: தமக்குத் துன்பம் செய்தவர்க்கும் இனிய நன்மைகளைச் செய்யாவிட்டால், ஒருவருடைய சால்பினால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the very purpose of nobility or perfection of character (சால்பு). It states that the true test of such greatness is responding to harm (இன்னா) with kindness. If a noble person cannot do good even to those who have wronged them, their nobility yields no real fruit (என்ன பயத்ததோ). The emphasis marker in இனியவே stresses that only sweet or good deeds should be returned for evil.

ai.literal: Poverty to a person disgrace is not, perfection called firmness to exist if obtained.
ai.translation: Poverty is no disgrace to a person, provided they possess the inner strength called perfect goodness.
ai.modern: சால்பு என்னும் மன உறுதி ஒருவரிடம் இருக்குமானால், வறுமை அவருக்கு ஒரு இழிவாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts material poverty with moral strength. The word 'இன்மை' (iṉmai) means lack or poverty, while 'இளிவு' (iḷivu) means disgrace. The text states that being poor is not a source of shame for a person, provided they possess 'திண்மை' (tiṇmai), meaning firmness or strength. Here, it refers specifically to the unwavering strength of 'சால்பு' (cālpu) or perfect goodness. Thus, true nobility lies in steadfast moral character, which completely overshadows any material deprivation.

ai.literal: Even if the aeon changes, they will not change, those who are called the ocean to perfection.
ai.translation: Those who are called the ocean of perfection will not change, even if the aeons themselves change.
ai.modern: உலகம் அழியும் ஊழிக்காலம் வந்து மாறினாலும், சான்றாண்மைக்குக் கடல் என்று சிறப்பிக்கப்படுபவர்கள் தம் நற்குணங்களிலிருந்து மாற மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares people of perfect character to an ocean, emphasizing their vastness and stability. The word 'ஊழி' refers to an aeon or the end of the world, a time of ultimate upheaval. Even if the entire world undergoes such a cataclysmic change, these noble individuals will not waver from their virtues. They are thus called the ocean ('ஆழி') of perfection ('சான்றாண்மைக்கு'), remaining steadfast and uncontainable in their goodness.

ai.literal: Noble ones' perfect goodness if decreases, vast earth itself will not bear, alas, burden.
ai.translation: If the perfect goodness of noble people diminishes, the vast earth itself will be unable to bear its burden.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்களின் சிறந்த பண்பு குறைந்துவிட்டால், இந்தப் பெரிய பூமியும் தன் பாரத்தைத் தாங்க முடியாமல் போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the foundational importance of noble character to the world. The word 'சான்றவர்' refers to those who are full of excellent qualities, and 'சான்றாண்மை' is their perfect goodness. The poet states that if such people lose their noble nature, the vast earth ('இருநிலம்') will no longer be able to bear its burden ('பொறை'). The particle 'மன்னோ' adds a tone of lament or certainty to this cosmic consequence. It implies that the moral weight of good people is what truly sustains the earth.
